Q: How do I strike a balance between email integration and keeping an IT ticket system lightweight? A:

I dont have a lot to add, thats how I would do it. The app can send notification mails. When you reply to a ticket update mail via mail, it should be added as a comment in the ticket. Provide user settings for receiving mails or not, maybe on a webapp wide scale and per project/ ticket/ update type. Provide sufficient search and filter tools on your webapp aswell so that people arent drawn to search in their mail client so easily - if thats a goal.

I dont know if you need a google mail account for that tho, should be possible with any server that can run a mail program probably.

So, in regards to your first point in what youre looking for: a normal web project should be fine. Sure, the database may get large quite fast but since youre a small company as you stated an average hosting instance is probably enough, maybe with a bit more space. Most of them come with good backup solutions as well. If you want be scalable for some reason, look at fancier providers.

Database optimization might be important here, know you indexes.

In regards to your second goal: code with performance in mind, optimize your database, dont pick unnecessary front end bloat.

Q: Send github actions->CI result to Slack A:

We are using slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.24.0 action in our github workflow

 - name: Send Slack message
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.24.0
        with:
          payload-file-path: slack-payload.json
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ env.QA_AUTOMATION_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}

Q: Vibe Coding Is Also Right Way? A:

Yes—vibe coding can be the right approach when used appropriately.

From my experience using Candor Data Platform, it significantly improves productivity by helping with code generation, debugging, and speeding up development cycles.

Vibe coding works especially well for:

  • Prototyping

  • Learning new concepts

  • Accelerating early-stage development

However, for areas like hardware control, real-time systems, and production-critical applications, structured engineering practices and proper validation are still essential.

In short, vibe coding is a powerful accelerator—but it works best when combined with discipline and verification
